title: Ina Garten's Roast Chicken
conventions: buy strings are cook measures (what goes in the pot). Grams are TARGET-scale: the mapper states them where its printed measure quantizes away from the exact scale, and otherwise they are parse-compute's source-basis weight for that line multiplied by scale_factor exactly once.

ingredients.notes: As purchased, giblets removed. Two birds roast in the same pan at this scale. REUSE, not a proposal: whole-chicken is a live commodity id at 7 of 7 stores. The missing vocabulary row is a naming question, not a registrar one (brown-lentils precedent). NOT rotisserie-chicken, which is cooked pulled meat, and not any breast row.

ingredients.buy: About 1 tablespoon salt and 2 teaspoons black pepper, to taste
ingredients.notes: Source gives no quantity ('season generously'); this is my estimate for two birds plus the vegetables. No quantity is given by the source, so the 2 tsp salt booked here is MY estimate for a 6 lb bird plus a pan of vegetables, with the matching black pepper on the buy string. Marked optional because the source treats it as season-to-taste.

ingredients.buy: 2 1/2 oz fresh thyme (about 3 large bunches), 35 sprigs of it left whole for the vegetables
ingredients.notes: Fresh, not dried. Most of it is stuffed in the cavity and discarded. A bunch and sprigs is unambiguously FRESH thyme; the board's dried-thyme near-miss is a form flip with a different price class and about three times the strength per gram. fresh-thyme is a live id at 4 of 7 stores. Bunch about 25 g plus 20 sprigs at ~1 g each.

ingredients.buy: 2 heads garlic, cut in half crosswise

ingredients.notes: Aromatic, stuffed and discarded. Rounded up from 1.75 to whole fruit. lemons is a live each-priced commodity. NOT lemon-juice, which is the bottled form flip and a different price class. House each-weight 100 g for a medium lemon; halved, stuffed and discarded, so its macros are near-immaterial.

ingredients.source_raw: 1 large yellow onion (sliced into large chunks)
ingredients.buy: 2 large yellow onions, cut into large chunks
ingredients.notes: House large-onion each-weight 170 g. Exact vocabulary row Yellow Onion [onions], 7 of 7 board. Not red-onion, which is a separate variety price class. House large-onion each-weight 170 g.

ingredients.source_raw: 1 bulb of fennel (tops removed, cut into wedges)
ingredients.buy: 2 fennel bulbs, tops removed, cut into wedges
ingredients.notes: Trimmed bulb weight. Fennel is stocked at only 1 of 7 stores - a carriage question, not a mapping one. Fresh bulb, NOT Ground Fennel seed (form flip, 345 vs 31 cal per 100 g and a spice-jar price class). The fennel commodity's unit is 'each', which is the fresh bulb, matching the existing Fennel Bulb macro row.
Topped off with pan drippings to make the gravy liquid.

Gravy roux. 7.8 g/tbsp. Exact vocabulary row; unqualified 'flour' in a butter roux is AP wheat flour, 7 of 7 board. Explicitly NOT the almond flour row, whose notes warn the flour commodity include pattern over-claims the bare term.

macro_cross_check.verdict: PASS AT THE EDGE, flagged twice. Calories agree within 4.2% and protein sits at -14.8%, just inside the 15% tolerance, so the 6 lb portion is right and no line needs re-examining. Both gaps run the same direction and have the same cause: I book the bird on an as-purchased basis with 30% bone removed, while the source appears to count more of the carcass as edible. FLAG 1: at 668 cal the computed figure is 18 cal over the run's 650 ceiling, even though the source's own 641 is inside it - and a roast bird leaves a great deal of rendered fat in the pan that this basis still counts, so the true value is likely at or under the source's. FLAG 2: the whole-chicken yield is a disclosed estimate. Carbohydrate is comfortable at 12 g against a 35 g ceiling.
